statements.__comment: Reset. This job is the only writer of exposure on load balancer resources. Iterative with a WHERE so every flagged node is reached, not only the first batch.
statements.query: MATCH (:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:GCPOrganization{id:$GCP_ORGANIZATION_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:GCPProject{id: $GCP_PROJECT_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(n) WHERE (n:GCPForwardingRule OR n:GCPProxy OR n:GCPUrlMap OR n:GCPSSLPolicy OR n:GCPBackendService OR n:GCPBackendBucket OR n:GCPInstanceGroup OR n:GCPNetworkEndpointGroup) AND (n.exposed_internet IS NOT NULL OR n.exposed_internet_type IS NOT NULL) WITH n LIMIT $LIMIT_SIZE REMOVE n.exposed_internet, n.exposed_internet_type return COUNT(*) as TotalCompleted

statements.__comment: An EXTERNAL / EXTERNAL_MANAGED forwarding rule is an internet-facing front door, whether or not its backends can be resolved.
statements.query:
MATCH (:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:GCPOrganization{id:$GCP_ORGANIZATION_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:GCPProject{id: $GCP_PROJECT_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(fr:GCPForwardingRule)
WHERE fr.load_balancing_scheme IN ['EXTERNAL', 'EXTERNAL_MANAGED']
SET fr.exposed_internet = true, fr.exposed_internet_type = ['external_load_balancer']

statements.__comment: Front end of those rules in the same project: the target proxy, the URL map behind an HTTP(S) proxy and the proxy's SSL policy (references resolved at ingestion, see compute.resolve_external_lb_backends).
statements.query:
MATCH (:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:GCPOrganization{id:$GCP_ORGANIZATION_ID})-[:OWNER]->(p:GCPProject{id: $GCP_PROJECT_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(fr:GCPForwardingRule)
WHERE fr.load_balancing_scheme IN ['EXTERNAL', 'EXTERNAL_MANAGED']
WITH p, collect(fr.target) AS targets, collect(fr.url_map) AS url_maps, collect(fr.ssl_policy) AS ssl_policies
MATCH (p)-[:RESOURCE]->(n)
WHERE (n:GCPProxy AND n.id IN targets) OR (n:GCPUrlMap AND n.partial_uri IN url_maps) OR (n:GCPSSLPolicy AND n.id IN ssl_policies)
SET n.exposed_internet = true, n.exposed_internet_type = ['external_load_balancer']

statements.__comment: Backends in the same project: backend services and backend buckets that an external rule reaches directly (SSL/TCP proxy, backend-service network LB) or through its URL map. Backends in another project (cross-project references) are not resolved.
statements.query:
MATCH (:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:GCPOrganization{id:$GCP_ORGANIZATION_ID})-[:OWNER]->(p:GCPProject{id: $GCP_PROJECT_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(fr:GCPForwardingRule)
WHERE fr.load_balancing_scheme IN ['EXTERNAL', 'EXTERNAL_MANAGED']
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:RESOURCE]->(um:GCPUrlMap) WHERE um.partial_uri = fr.url_map
WITH p, reduce(acc = [], refs IN collect(coalesce(fr.backend_services, []) + coalesce(um.services, [])) | acc + refs) AS refs
MATCH (p)-[:RESOURCE]->(n)
WHERE (n:GCPBackendService AND n.id IN refs) OR (n:GCPBackendBucket AND n.partial_uri IN refs)
SET n.exposed_internet = true, n.exposed_internet_type = ['external_load_balancer']

statements.__comment: Instance groups and network endpoint groups behind those backend services (set by the previous statement of this job): unmanaged groups and NEGs by id, managed groups by the instance group their manager runs. Every NEG type counts (VM, serverless, internet, hybrid, PSC): the NEG receives the internet traffic whatever sits behind it.
statements.query:
MATCH (:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:GCPOrganization{id:$GCP_ORGANIZATION_ID})-[:OWNER]->(p:GCPProject{id: $GCP_PROJECT_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(bs:GCPBackendService)
WHERE 'external_load_balancer' IN coalesce(bs.exposed_internet_type, [])
WITH p, reduce(acc = [], groups IN collect(coalesce(bs.backend_groups, [])) | acc + groups) AS groups
MATCH (p)-[:RESOURCE]->(g)
WHERE (g:GCPInstanceGroup AND (g.id IN groups OR g.instance_group IN groups)) OR (g:GCPNetworkEndpointGroup AND g.id IN groups)
SET g.exposed_internet = true, g.exposed_internet_type = ['external_load_balancer']

statements.__comment: A function behind one of those serverless NEGs keeps its own exposure decision (gcp_cloud_function_analysis.json, which runs earlier and resets it): the load balancer enforces the function's invoker IAM, so it is anonymously reachable only when anyone can invoke it. When that job already made it public, add 'external_load_balancer' as a second way in. Cloud Run and App Engine targets have no node; they stay recorded on the NEG.
statements.query:
MATCH (:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:GCPOrganization{id:$GCP_ORGANIZATION_ID})-[:OWNER]->(p:GCPProject{id: $GCP_PROJECT_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(neg:GCPNetworkEndpointGroup)-[:SERVERLESS_TARGET]->(fn:GCPFunction)<-[:RESOURCE]-(p)
WHERE 'external_load_balancer' IN coalesce(neg.exposed_internet_type, []) AND fn.exposed_internet = true
WITH DISTINCT fn
SET (CASE WHEN NOT 'external_load_balancer' IN coalesce(fn.exposed_internet_type, []) THEN fn END).exposed_internet_type = coalesce(fn.exposed_internet_type, []) + 'external_load_balancer'
